tyler-tanner: Wonderkid. Starboy. Hometown hero. Whatever you want to call him, Tanner is one of the best players in the nation. The Brentwood, Tennessee, native was recently named to the preseason AP All-America team — and for good reason.

As a sophomore, Tanner averaged 19.5 points, 5.1 assists and 2.4 steals per game. Better yet, in conference play alone, his averages jumped to 21.5 points, 5.5 assists and 2.3 steals — making him the only SEC player in the last 30 seasons to surpass the 21/5/2 marks. He received just about every accolade you could think of: All-SEC first team, SEC All-Defensive team and AP All-America honorable mentions from the Associated Press and USBWA.

The 6'0 guard set single-season Vanderbilt records in total steals (86) and total assists (184). He also became just the second player in Commodore history to score over 700 points in a season (702). In short, there is not much that Tanner has not proved so far. He is a top contender for the National Player of the Year award, and without a doubt the leader of this team.
ace-glass: Glass brings an impressive arsenal of three-level scoring from Washington State. He had a freshman season for the books for the Cougars last year. He set freshmen records for single-game scoring (40), single-season scoring (525), 3-pointers made (71) and free throw percentage (88.2%).

Overall, he averaged 16.4 points on 45.5% shooting from the field and 36.4% from behind the arc. Joining a team that just lost one of the best shooters in the country in Tyler Nickel, Glass will have his work cut out for him as a deep-range sniper. His bag runs much deeper than that, though, as he can get to the rim with impressive speed and use his dribble package to open up good looks for himself and others.

The Rancho Cucamonga, California, native will join Tanner in the backcourt, which has already begun to garner national attention. The impact of Glass’ scoring punch cannot be understated ahead of this season.
bangot-dak: Dak’s athletic build gives him the potential to be an elite rim-running, lob-catching and shot-blocking big man for the ’Dores. At Colorado in 2025-26, he averaged 11.5 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. His season-best performance came against Utah in early March, when he dropped 22 points, 10 rebounds and 4 blocks.

These blocks weren't a one-off occurrence — he led the Buffaloes in blocks as a sophomore (46) and a junior (50). Dak’s effectiveness went beyond shot blocking, as he recorded career-high performances in points (22), rebounds (13) and assists (6) last season.

The Lincoln, Nebraska, native stands at 6'11, 210 pounds with the speed of a guard. His ability to get up and down the floor will help him fit right into Byington’s system and make an immediate impact.
chandler-bing: The second of three returners on the roster, Bing showed serious flashes of potential as a significant contributor during his freshman season. The Atlanta native appeared in every game for the ’Dores in 2025-26, averaging 14.8 minutes per game — a tally that only went up throughout the season.

Bing’s averages do not tell the full story: He put up just 3.6 points and 1.6 rebounds on a nightly basis. But his defensive chops as a 6'6 guard with a strong frame are rare for a young player. He picked up seven steals and four blocks in conference play alone, contributing to his 18 total stocks (steals plus blocks) on the year.

Bing played 20 minutes in each of the team’s final eight games of the season, indicating internal growth and improved trust with Byington. As his minutes increased, his 3-point volume and efficiency did as well. This role, and the team’s reliance on Bing cashing in on open looks, is only set to increase in the upcoming season.
And before you ask, no, he has never watched Friends.
sebastian-williams-adams: Williams-Adams was highly recruited by Byington and the Vanderbilt staff — and nearly committed to the Black and Gold straight out of high school. Instead, he joined the Auburn Tigers in their first season under head coach Steven Pearl. As a freshman, he averaged 7.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 27.3 minutes per game.

The Tigers didn't see the same team success that Williams-Adams saw as an individual, which is likely part of the reason that he joined the Commodores. The Houston native was a top-50 overall player in the Class of 2025, and he showed why in his freshman campaign. His natural defensive abilities, strong build (6'9, 251 pounds) and long arms will make him an indispensable addition to the team.
berke-buyuktuncel: In an unprecedented move in the college basketball world, Buyuktuncel joined the Commodores over the summer after his former team, Nebraska, took down Vanderbilt in one of the best March Madness games in recent memory. With the Cornhuskers, he averaged 6.5 points and 5.6 rebounds, while also recording the fourth triple-double in Nebraska’s program history early in the season.

Standing at 6'10, 260 pounds, Buyuktuncel brings much-needed size to the Black and Gold. His impact as a shot-blocker will go a long way for a previously undersized team. The Bursa, Türkiye, native has also shown his willingness to fight on every single play through the ’Dores’ three exhibition games thus far. While he doesn't exactly fit the mold of a big man in a Byington-orchestrated system, there will be no shortage of effort with Buyuktuncel in the lineup.
t-o-barrett: Barrett had a few breakout games last season as a sophomore at Missouri but was behind Anthony Robinson and star guard/forward Mark Mitchell in the rotation. Despite this, he averaged 8.6 points and 3.0 assists — good for second on the team — while being one of just four Tigers to appear in all 33 games.

As a starter, Barrett averaged 12.4 points and 3.6 assists, showcasing his ability to rise to the occasion. He dropped a career-high 28 points against No. 22 Tennessee, going 12-for-17 from the field. The 6'6 guard recorded a career-high seven-assist, three-steal performance against Kentucky in the SEC Tournament. Needless to say, the Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, native will make the most of the opportunities that he gets off the bench in his new threads.
jayden-leverett: As a freshman, Leverett also saw his minutes increase throughout the season. He made the most of his playing time, impacting the game through hustle plays. Like Bing, this impact won't show up in the box score. He averaged just 1.0 points and 1.2 rebounds per game, which is hard to gauge since he only played over 10 minutes once last season.

What isn't hard to gauge, though, is his effort. Leverett secured a season-high five rebounds against Eastern Kentucky in November in just three minutes. He recorded three rebounds and a block in seven minutes against Florida in the semifinals of the SEC Tournament. He posted a stat line of five points, four rebounds and two steals on the road against Missouri in mid-February.

Leverett was the Commodores’ top performer back in September in an exhibition game against Virginia, but he still won't be a starter. He will, however, see an increased role as the team’s primary backup big man option. The El Paso, Texas, native will have many opportunities to make a name for himself off the bench in 2026-27.
ant-brown-jr: Hailing from Forestville, Maryland, Brown was named the top player in the Washington D.C. area by both 247Sports and On3 coming out of high school. Further, he was a consensus top-100 prospect and top-15 point guard in the Class of 2026. Brown has made the most of his opportunities through three exhibition games thus far — particularly against UAB, when he dropped a double-double with 10 points and 10 assists. The 6'3 freshman should continue to see real minutes backing up Tanner.
gabe-nesmith: After reclassifying from 2027 to 2026, Nesmith followed in his cousin Aaron Nesmith’s footsteps and came to play for the Commodores. The 6'6 wing averaged 16.4 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.2 steals per game in his final summer of the EYBL circuit. The Palm Beach, Florida, native showed impressive shot-making ability in Vanderbilt’s exhibition against Virginia before sitting out against UAB and Miami. Fans of the Black and Gold should be excited about Nesmith’s future after he just turned 18 last month.
ethan-mgbako: Mgbako was another consensus top-100 prospect, coming in as the No. 26 small forward in his class, according to 247Sports. The Somerset, New Jersey, native took his talents to a historic program in Virginia — Oak Hill Academy — that has produced numerous successful NBA players. Standing at 6'6, 210 pounds, Mgbako has a real chance to see legitimate playing time with his skill on the defensive side of the ball.
jackson-sheffield: Another highly touted recruit, Sheffield was a consensus four-star prospect and received a top-100 rating from two of the three major recruiting sites. The Hoover, Alabama, native was ranked as the No. 2 prospect in his state and was a consensus top-20 center in the Class of 2026. Sheffield, a 6'10, 241-pound big man, adds to the depth of Vanderbilt’s revamped frontcourt.
mavrick-hawkins: Hawkins played high school basketball at Pembroke Hill School in his hometown of Kansas City, Missouri. He was named Missouri Class 5 All-State, District Player of the Year and All-District as a junior. While he may sit toward the bottom of the rotation, he is deserving of a spot on the team with his history as an accomplished high school player.
baylor-allen: Staying close to home, Allen joined the Commodores as a native of Murfreesboro, Tennessee. He began his high school basketball journey at Providence Christian Academy in Murfreesboro before playing last season at IMG Academy. Similarly to Hawkins, he will likely reside on the end of the bench for the bulk of the season.
chase-byington: Byington, the son of Vanderbilt’s head coach, moved to Nashville, Tennessee, with his family two years ago. He played his final two high school seasons at Ensworth School in Nashville after beginning his career at Spotswood High School in Harrisonburg, Virginia. Byington nailed a 3-pointer in the Commodores’ outdoor exhibition against Virginia, eliciting quite the reaction from his teammates on the bench.
